lab_tests: EBV IgA serology (VCA-IgA, EA-IgA) — screening in high-risk populations
EBV DNA load (plasma) — tumor marker and prognostication

thresholds.biopsy: WHO Type II (non-keratinizing) or III (undifferentiated) — most common in southern China

clinical_features: Unilateral hearing loss / tinnitus / ear fullness (Eustachian tube obstruction)
Cranial nerve palsies (CN VI most common → diplopia)
diagnosis.gold_standard: Nasopharyngeal endoscopic biopsy with histopathological examination

treatment.indication: Primary treatment for all non-metastatic NPC (Stage I-IVA)

treatment.method: Induction chemotherapy (TPF: docetaxel + cisplatin + 5-FU) followed by CCRT

differential_diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of other head/neck sites
risk_factors: Salted fish consumption (IARC Group 1 carcinogen) — especially during childhood
prevention: EBV IgA serological screening in high-risk Cantonese populations (age ≥40, male, family history)
Reduction of salted fish consumption, especially in childhood

clinical_examples.description: A 52-year-old Cantonese male from Zhongshan, Guangdong, presents with a 3-month history of progressive right-sided nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, and a painless 3cm right upper cervical lymph node. He reports a family history of NPC (father). Nasopharyngeal endoscopy reveals a friable mass in the right fossa of Rosenmüller.
clinical_examples.key_findings: Cantonese male + painless cervical lymphadenopathy + nasal symptoms + EBV VCA-IgA 1:640 positive → high suspicion for NPC
clinical_examples.outcome: Biopsy confirmed WHO Type III undifferentiated NPC, Stage III (T2N2M0). Treated with induction TPF followed by concurrent cisplatin + IMRT. EBV DNA undetectable after treatment. 5-year disease-free survival in follow-up.
